title: k8s-node-provisioning-debug-scratchpad
content:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for debugging recent node provisioning failures in staging cluster (staging-us-west2).
- Symptoms: new nodes join but quickly go NotReady / kubelet crashloops / pods stuck in ContainerCreating. Intermittent attach/detach errors for PVs.

Timeline (rough):
- 2024-10-28 09:20 PT: automated ASG scaling created 3 new instances (ami: r-inference-ubuntu-2024-09).
- 09:22: nodes appear in kube API but status NotReady.
- 09:25: kubelet logs show TLS handshake / certificate rotation errors on node.
- 09:40: attempted cordon/drain + recreate, same behavior.

Commands tried / useful outputs:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  NAME                           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP
  ip-10-0-5-128.ec2.internal     NotReady   <none>   4m    v1.26.4   10.0.5.128

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-5-128.ec2.internal
  Conditions: KernelDeadlock False
              Ready        False  KubeletNotReady: kubelet stopped posting heartbeat
  Taints:      node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute for 5m

- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager  (snippets)
  Oct 28 09:19:40 ip-10-0-5-128 kubelet[2319]: E1028 09:19:40.123456   2319 server.go:256] TLS handshake error from "10.0.2.33:42012": remote error: tls: bad certificate
  Oct 28 09:19:41 ip-10-0-5-128 kubelet[2319]: E1028 09:19:41.654321   2319 server.go:231] failed to register node "ip-10-0-5-128.ec2.internal" with API server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

- cat /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet.crt | openssl x509 -noout -subject -dates  (shows cert expired/issued recently?)
- sudo systemctl status containerd
  Active: active (running)
- sudo crictl ps -a  -> container runtime healthy

- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep "kube-proxy|coredns|aws-ebs-csi"
  kube-proxy-...   Running   Node: ip-10-0-5-128   etc.
  aws-ebs-csi-controller-... Pending   because not enough nodes?

- kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-ip-10-0-5-128 (no centralized kubelet pods, looked at node journal instead)

- helm upgrade --install node-pool infra/node-pool --set image.tag=2024-09 --timeout 10m --namespace infra  (succeeded, but nodes still NotReady)

Hypotheses so far:
1) Kubelet certificate / provisioning hook is failing: x509 errors in the journal suggest kubelet can't present a CA-signed cert accepted by API server. Possibly cloud-init/user-data didn't populate correct join token or kubelet.conf has wrong CA path.
2) Time skew on new instances causing cert validation failures. Check ntp/chrony sync on new nodes.
3) Cgroup driver mismatch between kubelet and container runtime causing kubelet to fail later in bootstrap.
4) Cloud provider IAM / metadata access issue: kubelet unable to retrieve instance identity or attach/detach operations failing due to role.
5) AMI baked with older kubelet binary incompatible with control plane (v1.26.x mismatch or patched flags).

Quick checks to run on an affected node:
- sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env  (check kubelet args, --cgroup-driver)
- sudo cat /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf  (check server: https://api.staging.redwood.ai:6443 and client-certificate/data present)
- sudo timedatectl status  (check system clock)
- curl -sS --connect-timeout 5 "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/info" || true  (check metadata access)
- openssl s_client -connect api.staging.redwood.ai:6443 -showcerts  (verify API server cert chain from node)

Recent config changes to consider:
- New AMI now includes containerd 1.7.2 and kubelet 1.26.4. We recently removed a startup step that replaces /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt from S3 (we rely on kubeadm join to provision).
- Autoscaler policy changed to more aggressive scale-up on 10/25 -> more frequent cold starts; could expose timing issues in join scripts.

Repro steps (manual attempt):
1) Launch a t3.medium from same AMI in staging VPC with user-data debug logging enabled.
2) SSH, run the quick checks above.
3) Try to run kubeadm join --certificate-key=<redacted> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash=sha256:<hash> (simulate join path and capture output).

Errors seen during kubeadm join attempts:
- [WARNING IsDockerSystemdCheck]: failed to detect the docker systemd cgroup driver: Cgroup driver: cgroupfs
- error execution phase kubelet-start: could not initialize the kubelet: failed to get cluster info: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

Notes / clues from logs:
- /var/log/cloud-init-output.log shows a failed curl to S3 to download bootstrap script (curl: 28 Connection timed out) at about the same time instance was created. Network race possible (VPC NAT gateway scaling?)
- kube-proxy logs on node show flannel route not present -> CNI plugin may not be ready -> pods stuck at ImagePull or ContainerCreating even if runtime is up.

Immediate remediation attempts tried:
- Rebooting node -> no change
- Manually scp-ing the cluster CA cert to /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt and restarting kubelet -> kubelet progress: registers with API server for ~30s then later fails again with same TLS error (possible cert rotation race)
- Temporary workaround: launched nodes with older AMI (2024-06) and they joined fine. Points at AMI change as likely cause.

Next steps / action items:
- [ASAP] Roll back automated fleet to older AMI while we root cause. Coordinate with infra-sre to pause autoscaler. (assigned: Morgan)
- Verify cloud-init network fetch reliability: reproduce curl to S3 from new instance type across AZs. (assigned: me)
- Add debug logging to user-data to capture kubeadm join command & env before kubelet start.
- Check if we need to include static CA in AMI or ensure kubeadm join is run after network is fully up. Consider systemd unit with After=network-online.target + ExecStartPre checks.
- Hypothesis testing: deliberately skew node clock (or disable NTP) on a test instance to see if it reproduces x509 errors.
- Check kubelet startup flags for --provider-id / --cloud-provider and compare with control plane expectations.

References / useful commands to collect more data:
- kubectl -n kube-system get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 100
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=staging-node*" --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,State.Name,LaunchTime,Placement.AvailabilityZone]' --output table
- grep -i ebs /var/log/cloud-init-output.log ; journalctl -u kubelet | egrep "x509|certificate|handshake|TLS"

Notes to future self:
- Keep a copy of the last working AMI id in infra repo and add a quick rollback flag.
- Improve instrumentation on boot to emit join success/failure to CloudWatch (or our logging pipeline) so we can correlate network events.

If stuck escalate to SRE on-call with:
- Sample node ID, cloud-init logs, kubelet journal tail (last 200 lines), output of openssl s_client against API endpoint, and AMI id.

End of scratchpad.
